hypothesis: The measured 128-thread float2 mapping is the current strongest T3 result, while the valid 8-accumulator variant was slower than the 4-accumulator trial. Test a contrasting mapping with 64-thread CTAs: each lane owns four contiguous values within the same 256-element tile and uses float4 loads only for aligned, complete tiles, with guarded scalar handling for unaligned inputs and tails. Keep 1024 CTAs/partials, tile boundaries, and the 256-thread finalizer fixed. Whether wider per-thread work improves full-call time while meeting the FP64 error bound remains for controller measurement.
notes: This candidate keeps the two-stage fused topology, 1024 partials, 256-element CTA tile boundaries, and existing finalizer organization. It has not been measured; the controller should validate all required sizes and the stated FP64 error bound and measure full-call time.
transformations: Use a fused absolute-sum first stage with 1024 CTAs and 1024 partials, followed by the existing one-CTA, 256-thread finalizer.
Keep each CTA's 256-element global tile boundary and grid-stride progression, but use 64 threads with four contiguous elements per lane.
Use float4 loads only when the input pointer is 16-byte aligned and the tile is complete; use guarded scalar loads for unaligned input and partial tails.
Reduce per-thread sums with CUB and overwrite every partial and the final output on each call.
